title: A global quota, uneven traffic
description: A tenant has a soft global limit of 1,000 requests/minute across three regions, but 90% of its traffic comes from Europe. Splitting the limit equally throttles it well below its allowance. Checks must stay local and under 2 ms; small bounded over-admission is acceptable. What is the best fit?

options.text: Have every region enforce the full 1,000 requests/minute independently.
options.explanation: That allows up to three times the advertised quota. It is not a small, bounded approximation around the global limit.

options.text: Make each check synchronously consult counters in all three regions.
options.explanation: Synchronous cross-region coordination breaks the latency budget and couples availability to remote regions.

options.text: Enforce regional shares locally and rebalance them asynchronously using recent consumption.
options.explanation: Shares can follow the traffic without a remote call per request. State the sync interval and traffic-rate bound; a true global hard cap would require a different latency trade-off.

options.text: Keep equal shares and raise the client timeout so unused quota can accumulate.
options.explanation: A longer timeout does not move quota between regions. It only makes a slow limiter more expensive for callers.
